header: THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH, CIRCUIT COURT, HYDERABAD
[Deceased Shahzad Khan through L.Rs v. Learned VI-Addl. District Judge and others]
Applicants : Deceased Shahzad Khan through L.Rs.
Respondents No.1 & 2: Through Mr. Wali Muhammad Jamari,
body: MUHAMMAD HUMAYON KHAN, J.- Through this Civil Revision Application under section 115 C.P.C., the applicants, being the legal heirs of late Shahzad Khan, have called in question the order dated 12.08.2022 (the “impugned order”) passed by the learned VI-Additional District Judge/Model Civil Appellate Court-II, Hyderabad (the “learned Additional District Judge”), whereby their application for reconstruction of the record of Guardian Application No.29 of 1972, titled Mst. Fayyazi Begum v. Shahzad Khan (the “Guardian Application”), was dismissed.

2. Briefly, the facts giving rise to the instant revision are that Mst. Fayyazi Begum (respondent No.3, since deceased) instituted the Guardian Application in the Court of the District Judge, Hyderabad, with Shahzad Khan as the opponent. In 2013, respondents No.3 to 8 instituted F.C. Suit No.279 of 2013 (the “suit”) before the learned VI-Senior Civil Judge, Hyderabad, seeking declaration, partition, separate possession, mesne profits C.R.A No.226 of 2022 Page 2 of 10 and permanent injunction in respect of House No.424, Block-F, Latifabad, Hyderabad. They claimed the property as heirs of late Muhammad Shafi. Shahzad Khan was impleaded as a defendant and the applicants now contest the suit in his place. The applicants’ case is that in the Guardian Application, Mst. Fayyazi Begum had described respondents No.4 to 8 as the children of late Muhammad Sharif son of Gulab Khan. On that basis, they contend that the plaintiffs are estopped under Article 114 of the Qanune-Shahadat Order, 1984 (“QSO, 1984”), from claiming inheritance through Muhammad Shafi.

3. When the applicants applied for certified copies, the file of the Guardian Application could not be traced. Their application for reconstruction led to an inquiry through the learned V-Senior Civil Judge, Hyderabad and the report was submitted to the District Judge. The applicants state that the then District Judge, by order dated 21.01.2016, directed reconstruction of the record. According to them, however, the matter thereafter remained unattended for several years because one of the applicants was ill and their then counsel did not pursue it. On 04.03.2022, their new counsel applied for fresh notices to the respondents. The matter was transferred on 23.05.2022 to the learned Additional District Judge, who after hearing the parties, dismissed the application by the impugned order.

4. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the impugned order was passed without proper C.R.A No.226 of 2022 Page 3 of 10 consideration of the record. He argued that the statement of the applicants’ former counsel recorded during the inquiry on 28.08.2015 (Ex.3), together with the photocopies of the publication, guardian certificate and nikahnama produced with it, furnished sufficient material for reconstruction. He further submitted that the Institution Register of 1972 confirms that the Guardian Application was instituted; that the applicants rely upon that proceeding in their defence in the suit and that dismissal of the reconstruction application would cause them irreparable loss. He accordingly prayed that the impugned order be set aside and the matter remanded for a fresh decision.
5. Learned Assistant A.G., appearing for respondents No.1 and 2, supported the impugned order. No one appeared on behalf of respondents No.3 to 8.
6. Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned Assistant A.G. and perused the record.

7. The jurisdiction of this Court under section 115 C.P.C. is confined to cases where the subordinate Court has exercised a jurisdiction not vested in it by law, failed to exercise a jurisdiction so vested, or acted in the exercise of its jurisdiction illegally or with material irregularity. This Court, while exercising revisional jurisdiction, does not sit as a Court of appeal and cannot interfere merely because another view of the matter is possible. Without finally determining the question of maintainability of the instant C.R.A No.226 of 2022 Page 4 of 10 revision, I have examined whether the impugned order suffers from any such defect.

8. The learned Additional District Judge noted that the then Record Keeper had reported on 11.10.2007 that the file of the Guardian Application had been damaged by termites. The explanation was accepted by the then District Judge through Office Order dated 12.11.2007 and the inquiry into the missing or damaged record fixed responsibility on no one. Notice was thereafter issued to the other side, whose counsel filed photocopies of eight documents with a statement dated 19.07.2022. The learned Additional District Judge found that those documents had no connection with the Guardian Application, that the applicants had not produced any document establishing such a connection and that after the passage of about seven years, no material was available from which the file could be reconstructed. On that basis, the application was dismissed.

9. A Court may, in exercise of its inherent powers under section 151 C.P.C., reconstruct a judicial record which has been lost or destroyed, so that a party may not suffer on account of a loss for which it is not responsible. Such reconstruction must, however, be founded upon reliable material from which the contents of the original record can be ascertained with reasonable certainty. Certified copies, copies admitted by the opposite party and relevant records available in another Court or public office may furnish such material. Reconstruction, whether complete or partial, cannot be undertaken on conjecture, C.R.A No.226 of 2022 Page 5 of 10 nor can documents be incorporated into the reconstructed record without satisfactorily establishing that they formed part of the original proceedings.

10. In the instant case, the applicants have not shown that the finding of the learned Additional District Judge regarding the documents produced by the opposite party was erroneous. Although the impugned order does not separately discuss the photocopies of the publication, guardian certificate and nikahnama relied upon by the applicants, the omission, by itself, does not constitute a material irregularity warranting interference. Nothing has been brought on record to establish that those copies were verified against the original or certified record, or that they reliably reproduce the contents of the Guardian Application, the statements of the parties or the proceedings recorded therein. Even if genuine, those documents do not, by themselves, establish the particular statements which the applicants seek to rely upon in support of their plea of estoppel. The Institution Register establishes the institution of the Guardian Application in 1972, which is not disputed, but does not establish its contents. The applicants have themselves stated in the revision that their counsel informed the learned Additional District Judge on more than one occasion, including at the time of final arguments, that they had no material other than the documents already produced. In these circumstances, no sufficient ground has been made out for interference with the refusal to reconstruct the record. C.R.A No.226 of 2022 Page 6 of 10 11. It is also pertinent to note that damage to the file was reported in 2007, whereas the inquiry at the instance of the applicants was conducted in 2015. Though the applicants rely upon the order dated 21.01.2016, no further step appears to have been taken by them until March 2022. The explanations regarding illness and the inaction of their former counsel are not supported by material on record. The lapse of time is relevant to the availability of reliable material for reconstruction, though delay alone cannot justify refusal to reconstruct a record lost while in the custody of the Court.

12. The refusal to reconstruct the file does not, by itself, determine the applicants’ right to rely on admissible evidence concerning the Guardian Application in other proceedings. Article 76(c) of the QSO, 1984 permits secondary evidence where the original has been destroyed or lost or where it cannot be produced within a reasonable time for a reason not arising from the offering party’s own default or neglect. The record indicates that the file was damaged while in the custody of the Court and does not suggest that the loss was attributable to the applicants. The suit has since been decided by judgment and preliminary decree dated 08.08.2026. Any remedy available to the applicants against that judgment and decree must be pursued in accordance with law. The admissibility and evidentiary value of any material they may seek to rely upon, and the merits of their plea under Article 114 of the QSO, 1984, are matters for determination in the C.R.A No.226 of 2022 Page 7 of 10 appropriate proceedings. Neither the impugned order nor this order decides those questions.

13. I have also examined the record and proceedings of F.C. Suit No.279 of 2013, received from the learned Senior Civil Judge-I, Hyderabad, under letter No.1st Sr.C.J/HYD/-3058 of 2026 dated 18.11.2026 and the record and proceedings of the Guardian Application, received from the learned VI-Additional District Judge, Hyderabad, under letter No.VI/ADJ/HYD/-438 of 2026 dated 17.11.2026. The material placed before the Court shows that Muhammad Shafi son of Foujdar Khan was allotted D-Class House/Plot No.424, Block-F, measuring 150 square yards, situated at Unit No.8, Shah Latifabad, Hyderabad, under allotment order No.424-F VIII dated 13.05.1964. Following his death, the allotment was mutated in favour of his legal heirs, including Muhammad Shahzad, father of the applicant and respondents No.3 to 8. The applicant has produced the allotment order and the foti khata badal entry as Annexure-F and a legal-heirship certificate of Muhammad Shafi son of Foujdar Khan as Annexure E. These documents show that the persons named therein were recorded as Muhammad Shafi’s legal heirs. The record further shows that the dispute over their respective entitlement arose after the death of Muhammad Shahzad and in the course of the suit instituted by Mst. Fayyazi Begum and the other plaintiffs. No finding on the parties’ respective shares is called for in this revision. C.R.A No.226 of 2022 Page 8 of 10 14. There is yet another material aspect of the case. This revision was filed on 03.10.2022, when the suit was pending, and prayer clause (ii) was made at that stage. The record shows that the suit was transferred to the Court of the learned Senior Civil Judge-I, Hyderabad and was decided by judgment and preliminary decree dated 08.08.2026, after evidence had been recorded, during the pendency of this revision. The record also refers to an application before the Assistant Commissioner challenging the legal-heirship certificate produced as Annexure E and F.C. Suit No.345 of 2013, in which the applicant acted as attorney for his mother; those proceedings were dismissed. Prayer clause (ii), seeking a stay of the proceedings of the suit, is reproduced below:

“ii. That this Honourable Court may be pleased to stay the proceedings of F.C. Suit No.279 of 2013 pending before the Court of the learned VI-Senior Civil Judge, Hyderabad, till the final disposal of this Revision Application.”

15. Consequently, prayer clause (ii) became infructuous upon disposal of the suit on 08.08.2026. However, on both dates of hearing, i.e. 04.11.2026 and 18.11.2026, learned counsel for the applicants did not bring this subsequent development to the notice of this Court. The prayer for stay was made when the suit was admittedly pending; therefore, no adverse inference can be drawn merely from its inclusion in the revision as originally filed. Nevertheless, the disposal of the suit was a material subsequent development which ought to have been disclosed by learned counsel. Such omission is not C.R.A No.226 of 2022 Page 9 of 10 appreciated. The revision, however, is being decided on its own merits.

16. In view of the above discussion, no jurisdictional defect, illegality or material irregularity in the impugned order has been established. A remand would serve no useful purpose, particularly when the applicants stated before the learned Additional District Judge that they had no further material to produce. The suit has also been decided and the relief sought in prayer clause (ii) is no longer available. The observations of the learned Additional District Judge and of this Court concerning the documents are confined to the application for reconstruction. They shall not be treated as findings on the genuineness, relevance or admissibility of any document in any proceedings or on the merits of any appeal or other remedy pursued in accordance with law against the judgment and preliminary decree dated 08.08.2026.

17. For the foregoing reasons, the instant Civil Revision Application is dismissed along with the pending application(s), if any, with costs of Rs.100,000/- (Rupees one hundred thousand only), imposed upon the applicants in view of the omission noted in paragraph 15 above. The amount shall be deposited with the Additional Registrar of this Court within period of fifteen (15) days, who shall disburse the same for a suitable welfare purpose of the High Court, including its library or clinic, as deemed appropriate. Let a copy of this order be communicated to the learned VI-Additional District Judge, Hyderabad, and C.R.A No.226 of 2022 Page 10 of 10 the learned Senior Civil Judge-I, Hyderabad, for information, and their respective records and proceedings be returned forthwith. It is clarified that this order shall not prejudice any remedy available to the parties under the law against the judgment and preliminary decree dated 08.08.2026, nor shall it affect their respective rights and defences in such proceedings.
